name: sentry
description: Investigate Sentry issues, events, releases, monitors and replays
long_description: Bring a Sentry personal, organization or internal integration token for a US-region organization on sentry.io. The gateway keeps the token off your Sprite and sends it as a bearer token. Saving or testing it checks its scopes through GET /api/0/. A Sprite can list organizations, projects and teams, investigate issues and events, run Discover queries and read releases, cron monitors, check-ins, replays and dashboards. Issue operations and project settings are read-only. With additional scopes, a Sprite can also manage releases and cron monitors, create deploys and submit user feedback. Grant only the scopes the Sprite needs. Sentry's API is free to call within its rate limits.

messages.400: Sentry rejected the request (%{status}); check the query parameters and body
messages.403: This Sentry token lacks the scope for this request; create a token with the scope the endpoint documents
messages.404: Not found in Sentry; check the organization and project slugs and that the organization is in the US region
messages.429: Sentry rate limit reached for this endpoint; wait for X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-Reset or Retry-After and retry
messages.provider_unreachable: Could not reach Sentry; retry later

presentation.tagline: Investigate Sentry issues and read events, releases and monitors from a Sprite without putting the token on it.
presentation.setup: In Sentry, open Personal Tokens (sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/) and create a token with only the scopes the Sprite needs. Start with org:read, project:read and event:read. Add project:releases if you need to create releases or deploys. Organization tokens and internal integration tokens also work. Use a token for a US-region organization.

notices.title: Billing
notices.body: Sentry's API has no per-request charge. Saving or testing the token reads `GET /api/0/`, which returns the token's own scopes. Sentry rate limits each caller per endpoint and answers 429 when exceeded; the `X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-*` headers are passed back. Sentry asks integrations not to poll: prefer wide queries over tight loops.

notices.title: Scope
notices.body: Read organizations, projects, teams, environments, repositories, issues, events, Discover results, releases, cron check-ins, replays and dashboards. Issue operations and project settings are read-only. The gateway allows writes for releases, deploys, cron monitors and user feedback. It blocks member and invite management, token and DSN management, service hooks, Sentry apps, SCIM and alert rules. Sentry enforces the token's scopes for each allowed route.

notices.title: Smallest scopes
notices.body: Use `org:read`, `project:read` and `event:read` for read-only use. Add `project:releases` for releases and deploys, `alerts:write` for cron monitor changes, or `project:write` for legacy user feedback only if the Sprite needs those operations. Sentry returns 403 when a request exceeds the token's permissions.

notices.title: US region only
notices.body: This connector talks to `sentry.io`, the host Sentry documents for organizations whose data is stored in the US. Organizations in the EU region are served from `de.sentry.io`, and self-hosted Sentry runs on your own host; neither is covered by this connector.

usage_notes: Sentry paths end with a slash (`/api/0/organizations/`); without it Sentry redirects. JSON bodies need `Content-Type: application/json`.

The forwarded `Link` header contains Sentry URLs. For `rel="next"` with `results="true"`, replace the query string on your original gateway URL with the full query string from that link, including `cursor`. Keep the gateway host and path so it can attach your token. Stop when the next link is missing or has `results="false"`.
Release versions may contain `.`, `@`, `+` and `-` (`my-app@1.2.3+build`) and pass the connector's path rule; a version containing `/` cannot be addressed in a path.
